entries.title: Proverbs 7:2
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Live - Thou shalt live. Eye - With all possible care and diligence.

entries.title: Proverbs 7:3
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Bind them - As a ring which is continually in a man's eye.

entries.title: Proverbs 7:4
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: And call - Acquaint and delight thyself with her.

entries.title: Proverbs 7:8
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Passing - Idle and careless, near the corner of the street in which her house stood.

entries.title: Proverbs 7:12
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Without - Without the door of her house. Corner - Of the streets, where she might either conceal or discover herself, as she saw fit.

entries.title: Proverbs 7:14
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Offerings - I have paid my peace - offerings which I had vowed. Whereby she signifies, that she had plentiful provisions at her house for his entertainment. For the peace - offerings were to be of the best flesh, Lev 22:21 , and a considerable part of these offerings fell to the offerer's share.

entries.title: Proverbs 7:20
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Hath taken - Which is an evidence that he designs to stay a considerable time. At the day - So that we need not fear any surprise.

entries.title: Proverbs 7:22
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: As an ox - Going to it securely, as if it were going to a good pasture.

entries.title: Proverbs 7:23
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: His liver - His vital parts, 'till his life be lost.
